Test Your Agent Memory Cutoff: It Can Drop Required Rules
A Cosine Cutoff Can Silently Drop Agent Memory Constraints
presentation.title_rationale: The selected title leads with the product area (agent memory cutoffs), names the reader problem in six words (cutoffs can hide constraints), and promises the one thing the article actually delivers: a measurement you can repeat on your own facts before picking a number. It drops the 2026 label and the method-heavy clause from the headline, both of which are stated in the introduction, and it makes no claim beyond the recorded fixture result that a per-embedder cutoff deleted a stored rule.
presentation.visual_purpose: A three-step conceptual checklist - constraint query, similarity score, threshold decision - showing where a cutoff can remove a stored rule. It is a diagram of the pathway the article measures, not a plot: it carries no scores or percentages, and the footer states it is a conceptual checklist and not new measurement data. Magnitudes stay in the article's tables and the raw run record.
